components.title: The Water Cycle
components.subtitle: Journey of water through evaporation, condensation, and precipitation.

components.title: Overview
components.text: Water is constantly moving on Earth. It changes from liquid to gas to solid, recycling itself through a continuous global journey driven by the sun.

components.label: EVAPORATION & TRANSPIRATION
components.title: Lifting Water into the Sky
components.body: Heat from the sun warms water in oceans, lakes, and rivers, causing it to evaporate into water vapour. Plants also release moisture from their leaves through a process called transpiration.
components.takeaway: Solar energy powers the upward movement of water vapour into the atmosphere.

components.label: CONDENSATION
components.title: Forming Clouds
components.body: As warm water vapour rises, it cools and condenses into tiny liquid water droplets or ice crystals around microscopic particles in the air, forming clouds and fog.
components.takeaway: Cooling air forces water vapour to transition back into liquid droplets, creating clouds.

components.label: PRECIPITATION & COLLECTION
components.title: Returning to Earth
components.body: When water droplets in clouds become too heavy to stay suspended, they fall back to Earth as rain, snow, sleet, or hail. This water collects in oceans, rivers, and underground aquifers, ready to start the cycle again.
components.takeaway: Gravity pulls condensed moisture downward, completing the continuous cycle.

components.label: WORKED EXAMPLE
components.title: Puddle Disappearance
components.body:
Have you ever noticed a puddle disappearing on a sunny day after rain? 

1. Heat from the sun warms the puddle water.
2. Water molecules absorb energy and escape into the air as invisible vapour.
3. Within hours, the puddle is completely dry.
components.code:
# Simulated Puddle Evaporation Rate
sunlight_intensity = 0.85 # High
initial_volume_liters = 2.5
evaporation_rate_per_hour = 0.5

hours_to_dry = initial_volume_liters / evaporation_rate_per_hour
print(f"Puddle dries in approximately {hours_to_dry} hours.")
components.code_caption: Python simulation of solar evaporation over time.
components.takeaway: Evaporation happens every day at ambient temperatures, not just at boiling point.

questions.question: What primary energy source drives the entire water cycle?
questions.explanation: Solar energy provides the heat required for evaporation and atmospheric currents.

questions.question: What is the process called when plants release water from their leaves?
questions.explanation: Transpiration is the release of water vapour from plant leaves into the atmosphere.

questions.question: Which phase change occurs during condensation?
questions.explanation: Condensation turns warm water vapour (gas) into cooler water droplets (liquid).
